title: Create Accessibility Regression Harness for Themed Buttons and Table Row Variants (VPAT Evidence)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Establish an automated regression harness and manual test checklist that validates keyboard navigation, ARIA semantics, and contrast for the new theme tokens applied to Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost) and Table row variants (default/compact/selected/highlighted). Produce VPAT-compliant evidence artifacts and a single-source Confluence playbook for ongoing audits.
background: Recent token updates introduced dynamic color aliases and a new compact row density. Early adopter teams reported inconsistent focus outlines and low-contrast hover states on ghost buttons. There is no current automated capture of screenreader text or keyboard flow for these component permutations; VPAT evidence is scattered across PR comments. We need reproducible test cases to avoid regressions and streamline future audits.
proposed_work: Design and implement a Cypress + axe-core test suite that covers keyboard focus order, skip-to behavior, and ARIA attributes for button groups and table rows across theme tokens.
Add a headless screenreader capture step (NVDA via CI container shim for Windows or Orca capture for Linux) to collect spoken output for representative flows.
Create visual contrast assertion scripts using an image-diff baseline for hover/active/focus states at 1x and 2x densities.
Author a VPAT evidence template (Confluence) that maps each WCAG success criterion to our test case IDs and artifacts.
Prototype a Figma checklist for designers to validate token pairings before token PRs merge.
acceptance_criteria: Automated suite runs in CI (design-system-a11y job) and fails the build when critical keyboard or contrast regressions are detected.
At least 25 permutations covered: 3 button intents × 3 sizes × 3 token themes + 4 table row states × 3 densities.
Screenreader capture artifacts exist for 10 representative flows and are attached to the VPAT page.
VPAT Confluence page created with mapped test IDs, links to CI artifacts, visual diffs, and a maintainer checklist.
Design team signoff on Figma checklist and two sample runs demonstrating regression detection.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Headless screenreader capture in CI is flaky across OS images. Mitigation: Start with a hermetic NVDA capture on Windows self-hosted runner and fallback to manual capture steps for Linux.
Risk: Visual diffs sensitive to small rendering differences (antialiasing). Mitigation: use perceptual diff thresholds and baseline normalization using same browser/viewport in CI.
Risk: Test suite runtime increases CI duration. Mitigation: run full suite nightly and a fast smoke gate on PRs (critical permutations only).
design_decisions: Choose axe-core for accessibility assertions and supplement with custom ARIA checks where axe misses nuanced keyboard scenarios.
Treat VPAT artifacts as single-source-of-truth in Confluence; CI artifact links will be immutable by date-tagging runs.
Only block PRs on P0/P1 regressions; non-critical contrast deviations will open automated tickets for designers.
